text.p: - The Clinton-Yeltsin summit in Helsinki will demonstrate that Russia's status has weakened significantly, Russian and American journalists say.
- Russia's first deputy prime minister Anatoly Chubais will try to cut a deal with miners in Kemerovo to blunt a national day of action set for March, 27.
- Instead of going to Helsinki with President Yeltsin, Anatoly Chubais is flying to Kemerovo in an attempt to defuse tensions there.
- The newly appointed first deputy prime minister Boris Nemtsov will have to resist powerful industrial and regional lobbys in the government.
- Despite serious disagreements between Russa and U.S., Helsinki may once again become a symbol of cooperation in Europe.
- On the eve of Russia's nationwide strike the authorities are receiving alarming signals from different regions.
- We should be resolute and brave on March 27, says the headline of the pro-communist paper which actively supports the day of action.
- President Clinton has injured his knee on the eve of the summit but it is Russia that is on its knees now.
